findings.title: NPE when fallback all-clients resource is missing in per-client permission check
findings.body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when no resource exists for the specific client, the code replaces `resource` with the result of getResourceTypeResource(..., CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) but never checks it for null. If that synthetic 'Clients' resource is absent (for example the admin-permissions realm was enabled/initialized before the new client resource type existed, or the resource was removed), findByResource(server, resource) at this line dereferences null and the request fails with a NullPointerException (HTTP 500) instead of denying the permission. Add a null check and return false.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission returns the synthetic all-clients resource name 'Clients' as a client ID
findings.body: resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) matches both individual client resources and the synthetic all-clients resource whose name is "Clients" because AdminPermissionsSchema.init creates that resource with type "Clients". If an all-clients scope permission exists, hasGrantedPermission returns true for it and granted.add(resource.getName()) adds "Clients" to the returned Set<String>. Callers expect client IDs, so the set is polluted with a non-existent ID. Exclude resource.getName().equals(AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) or otherwise skip the type-level resource.

findings.title: Role/client/group removal listener can call V2 unsupported methods when both fine-grained authz features are enabled
findings.body: The listener is gated on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ only, but AdminPermissions.management(...) gives precedence to ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. If both features are enabled, RoleRemovedEvent/ClientRemovedEvent/GroupRemovedEvent still enter the block and management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2. For clients, MgmtPermissionsV2.clients().setPermissionsEnabled(...) throws UnsupportedOperationException, so deleting a client (and similarly roles/groups if their V2 implementations are unsupported) can fail with an exception. The feature guard should account for V2 being active or the listener should force the V1 management implementation.

findings.title: Javadoc says void requireView() returns boolean
findings.body: The newly added Javadoc for `void requireView()` says 'Returns true if canView() returns true' even though the method returns void and throws ForbiddenException when not permitted. The same wording problem exists for requireViewClientScopes(). This misdocuments the API and can confuse implementers; adjust the Javadoc to describe the throw/require behavior instead of a boolean return.
